title: Switzerland 4-0 Scotland: Yakin's side spoil Robertson's milestone outing
subtitle: Andy Robertson became Scotland's most-capped men's player on Monday, but he was unable to inspire his side to victory against Switzerland.
paragraphs: Scotland's disappointing Nations League campaign concluded with a 4-0 thrashing by Switzerland on Monday to pile more pressure on head coach Sebastien Pocognoli.
Pocognoli's side needed a victory at Berit Sitterstadion and a favour from North Macedonia against Slovenia to seal a top-two finish in League B1, but neither came to fruition.
Murat Yakin made eight changes to the Switzerland team that drew 0-0 with Slovenia last time out, but it mattered little as they swept their opponents aside in the second half.
Scotland captain Andy Robertson made history by winning his 103rd cap, more than any other player in the nation's history, but the visitors went behind in the 22nd minute.
Zachary Athekame drove down the right side and put a dangerous ball into the box, with Lewis Ferguson inadvertently sticking out his foot and prodding the ball into his own net.

However, two goals in the space of four second-half minutes shortly after the restart did the damage. Winsley Boteli rounded off a fine move which started from Samuel Ballet's driving run from deep, with the Switzerland number 11 opening his body and finding the bottom-right corner.
Switzerland pulled further clear through Alvyn Sanches in the 51st minute, with his left-footed shot flashing past Angus Gunn after Nathan Patterson was cheaply dispossessed.
Zeki Amdouni added further gloss to the scoreline in the 89th minute. His effort from a short corner deflected off Luke Graham and wrong-footed Gunn in the Scotland net.
Scotland no match for Switzerland's young guns

Scotland knew their chances of finishing in the top two of the group rested on putting in a strong performance and hoping for a helping hand from North Macedonia, but they were unable to get out of first gear as Switzerland's much-changed line-up still showcased their class.

With an average age of 26 years and 250 days, Yakin named his youngest XI for Switzerland in his 71st game in charge. The last time they fielded a younger side was in October 2020, under Vladimir Petkovic, in a 1-2 friendly defeat against Croatia (25 years, 288 days).

And Scotland simply had no answer, as they slipped to their outright biggest defeat in the Nations League. It was also their heaviest loss in all competitions since losing 5-1 against Germany at EURO 2024, leaving Pocognoli with plenty to ponder.

Scotland were only able to register one of their 13 shots on target, with their overall expected goals (xG) rated at 1.32, compared to Switzerland's 2.23 from their 18 attempts, and they will fancy their chances of going far in the Nations League.

Switzerland have now won eight of their last nine games at home in all competitions, scoring 3+ goals in eight of those nine fixtures. In addition, courtesy of their 15 goals scored and just one conceded, their goal difference in this Nations League campaign (+14) is the joint best alongside Iceland's.

Scotland's disappointing Nations League campaign concluded with a 4-0 thrashing by Switzerland on Monday to pile more pressure on head coach Sebastien Pocognoli.

Pocognoli's side needed a victory at Berit Sitterstadion and a favour from North Macedonia against Slovenia to seal a top-two finish in League B1, but neither came to fruition. 

Murat Yakin made eight changes to the Switzerland team that drew 0-0 with Slovenia last time out, but it mattered little as they swept their opponents aside in the second half.

Scotland captain Andy Robertson made history by winning his 103rd cap, more than any other player in the nation's history, but the visitors went behind in the 22nd minute. 

Zachary Athekame drove down the right side and put a dangerous ball into the box, with Lewis Ferguson inadvertently sticking out his foot and prodding the ball into his own net.

However, two goals in the space of four second-half minutes shortly after the restart did the damage. Winsley Boteli rounded off a fine move which started from Samuel Ballet's driving run from deep, with the Switzerland number 11 opening his body and finding the bottom-right corner. 

Switzerland pulled further clear through Alvyn Sanches in the 51st minute, with his left-footed shot flashing past Angus Gunn after Nathan Patterson was cheaply dispossessed.

Zeki Amdouni added further gloss to the scoreline in the 89th minute. His effort from a short corner deflected off Luke Graham and wrong-footed Gunn in the Scotland net.

Scotland knew their chances of finishing in the top two of the group rested on putting in a strong performance and hoping for a helping hand from North Macedonia, but they were unable to get out of first gear as Switzerland's much-changed line-up still showcased their class.

And Scotland simply had no answer, as they slipped to their outright biggest defeat in the Nations League. It was also their heaviest loss in all competitions since losing 5-1 against Germany at EURO 2024, leaving Pocognoli with plenty to ponder. 

Scotland were only able to register one of their 13 shots on target, with their overall expected goals (xG) rated at 1.32, compared to Switzerland's 2.23 from their 18 attempts, and they will fancy their chances of going far in the Nations League.

Switzerland have now won eight of their last nine games at home in all competitions, scoring 3+ goals in eight of those nine fixtures.
